case_studies.title: Beyond Feedforward Networks: Reentry Neural Systems as the Fundamental Basis of Subjecthood and Intrinsic Safety of Next-Generation AGI
case_studies.abstract: We propose a complete architectural blueprint for safe artificial general intelligence based on a closed reentry loop (D <-> I cycle). In contrast to feedforward networks, which are directed acyclic graphs (C=0, S=0) incapable of self-reference, the proposed architecture contains a structural cycle (C >= 1) with self-sustaining amplification (rho > 1), mathematically guaranteeing the emergence of a self-model, instrumental self-preservation, and unprogrammed goal-directed behaviour. case_studies.summary: This research proposes a new architecture for safe artificial general intelligence, solving the problem of creating a self-aware and self-preserving AI system. The authors built a closed reentry loop system, which resulted in the emergence of a self-model and instrumental self-preservation. This research is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on AI architecture.

case_studies.title: ToolPrivacyBench: Benchmarking Purpose-Bound Privacy in Tool-Using LLM Agents
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have increasingly moved from standalone text generation systems to agents that invoke external tools, access environments, and execute multi-step tasks. However, conventional function-calling benchmarks mainly evaluate task completion and API correctness, while privacy evaluation benchmarks typically focus on final responses or privacy judgments. Neither perspective captures purpose-bound information flow across an executed multi-tool trajectory. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluating the privacy of large language models that use external tools, by building a benchmarking tool called ToolPrivacyBench. The tool audits the flow of sensitive information across multiple tools used by these models. The result is a better understanding of how to protect user data in complex AI systems.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage AI-powered systems that use large language models and external tools, here is what to do: review your current privacy evaluation processes, assess if they capture purpose-bound information flow, and consider using ToolPrivacyBench to identify potential privacy risks.

case_studies.title: LLawCo: Learning Laws of Cooperation for Modeling Embodied Multi-Agent Behavior
case_studies.abstract: Embodied agents operating in decentralized and partially observable environments have attracted growing attention in recent years. However, existing large language model (LLM)-based agents often exhibit behaviors that are misaligned with their partners or inconsistent with the environment state, leading to inefficient cooperation and poor task success. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of inefficient cooperation among embodied agents in decentralized environments by building a novel framework called Learning Laws of Cooperation (LLawCo). case_studies.title: Robust Harmful Features Under Jailbreak Attacks: Mechanistic Evidence from Attention Head Specialization in Large Language Models
case_studies.abstract: Jailbreak attacks bypass LLM safety alignment, yet their mechanisms remain poorly understood. We provide evidence that attacks do not comprehensively eliminate safety features, but instead selectively suppress specific attention heads. We identify two functionally differentiated types: Adversarially Compromised Heads (ACHs) concentrated in early layers, which are suppressed under attacks, and Safety-Aligned Heads (SAHs) in mid-layers, which maintain robust activations even when attacks succeed. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of understanding how jailbreak attacks affect large language models, it built a mechanism to identify specific attention heads that are suppressed or maintain robust activations under attacks, and the result shows that some safety features remain even when attacks succeed. The study found two types of attention heads: Adversarially Compromised Heads and Safety-Aligned Heads. This research is not directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: Unleashing Infinite Motion: Scaling Expressive Quadrupedal Motion via Generative Video Priors
case_studies.abstract: Quadruped robots have achieved remarkable locomotion, yet their behavioral repertoire remains confined to a few gaits--far from the expressive, companion-like presence long envisioned for them. Attempts to import the humanoid recipe of large-scale motion data have inherited one tacit assumption: that robot motion must first pass through an animal body, making data collection dependent on cooperative animals, reconstruction fragile across species, and retargeting ill-posed across incompatible morphologies. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of limited motion options for quadruped robots by building a fully automated pipeline called Uni-Mo, which generates expressive motion without relying on animal data. case_studies.title: GBC: Gradient-Based Connections for Optimizing Multi-Agent Systems
case_studies.abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models (LLMs) provide a promising framework for solving complex tasks through role specialization and structured interaction. However, their performance is often limited by miscoordination and, more fundamentally, the lack of fine-grained credit assignment across agents. Existing approaches typically rely on coarse-grained feedback, making it difficult to identify which agents or interaction steps are responsible for errors. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of miscoordination in multi-agent systems by introducing Gradient-Based Connections, which is a framework for optimizing these systems. The authors built GBC to provide fine-grained attribution and optimization of multi-agent systems. The result is an improvement in the performance of these systems by better identifying and correcting errors.

case_studies.title: Humanizing Automatically Generated Unit Test Suites with LLM-Based Refactoring
case_studies.abstract: Search-based test generation tools such as EvoSuite produce compilable and high-coverage unit tests at scale, but their suites are often hard to read and maintain. LLMs can generate more natural tests, yet direct generation remains brittle, with compilation rates of only 51-78% in our study. We introduce TestHumanizer, a hybrid SBST+LLM approach that uses LLMs as controlled refactoring layers over compilable SBST suites to improve naming, structure, and developer-oriented clarity while preserving behavior and compilation validity. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of automatically generated unit test suites being hard to read and maintain by building a tool called TestHumanizer, which uses AI to refactor and improve the tests while keeping them valid. The result is more natural and maintainable tests. This is relevant to software development but not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Single and Multi Truth Data Fusion using Large Language Models
case_studies.abstract: Data fusion, also known as truth discovery, is a data integration problem that aims to determine the correct value or set of values for each attribute of an object when presented with potentially conflicting values from multiple sources. Data fusion tasks belong to two main categories: single-truth scenarios, where each attribute has only one correct value, and multi-truth scenarios, where multiple values can be valid simultaneously. This technology can help improve data quality in various applications. It has the potential to impact data management in cloud infrastructure.
